sections.h2: Where to take care of tax business
sections.html:
Taylor County stacks its tax offices on one street in Campbellsville. The sheriff, the Property Valuation Administration (PVA) and the county clerk all work out of 203 North Court Street, so a single stop can cover a payoff, an exemption form and a lien check.

Taylor County tax offices in Campbellsville
OfficeSuite and hoursPhone
Sheriff, current billsSuite 7; Monday to Friday 8:00 to 4:30; a drop box sits outside the door(270) 465-4351
PVA, values and exemptionsSuite 6; Monday to Friday 8:00 to 4:30(270) 465-5811
County clerk, delinquent bills and recordingMonday to Friday 8:00 to 4:30; Saturday 9:00 to noon(270) 465-6677

The sheriff's page also links an online portal for searching and paying 2026 bills. Pop-ups must be switched on in your browser or the portal will not open.

Campbellsville is the seat and the only city, with Acton, Hobson, Mannsville, Saloma and Spurlington among the unincorporated communities. Marion, Casey, Adair, Green and LaRue counties surround the county, which covers 277 square miles, 266 of them land. Campbellsville Independent and Taylor County Schools split the school districts, and Campbellsville University anchors the local economy.

The county has 26,763 residents as of July 2025, a 2.8 percent gain on 2020, and 11,247 housing units. Typical home value is $174,200 and typical rent is $718. Owners live in 68.8 percent of units, so a good share of the market is rentals: the 2020 count found 35.9 percent of occupied units rented, and 28.9 percent of households were one person living alone.

Owners with a mortgage pay a median $1,217 a month for housing, against $432 for owners with none. Household income is $60,456 and the mean commute is 22.7 minutes. Just 9 building permits were issued in 2025, so new construction adds little to the supply, and existing houses make up most of what sells.

Households average 2.45 people, so many homes are small ones. About one resident in five is past 65 (19.5 percent). That group is the likeliest to use the homestead break described below. Landlords will see a different picture: the rental vacancy rate was 5.8 percent in 2020, and 9.2 percent of all housing units stood vacant.

State law sends payment to the sheriff, with a due date at the end of the assessment year. The sequence runs:

  • A bill settled by November 1 earns a 2 percent break.
  • Between that date and December 31, the printed amount applies.
  • January brings a 5 percent surcharge.
  • After January 31, 10 percent applies, with the sheriff's add-on fee from the Revenue Department's delinquency worksheet.

Taylor County bills turn delinquent on April 15 each year, when the sheriff's file closes and unpaid bills pass to the clerk.

sections.h2: If your bill is past due
sections.html:
Act before April 15 if you can, because that date moves the file from the sheriff to the clerk and adds commissions. After that, the county attorney's letters begin, and each notice gives you another chance to pay before a company can buy the bill. Calling the clerk at (270) 465-6677 tells you where your parcel stands in that sequence.

Owners who are selling should not wait for the sale date at all. A bill that has been bought by an outside company has to be settled with that company, and its costs are higher than the clerk's. Settling early keeps the closing on schedule and keeps more of your proceeds.

sections.h2: What the clerk does with unpaid bills
sections.html:
Collection moves to the clerk, with the county attorney writing to each owner. Two letters go out and the delinquent list runs in the Central Kentucky News Journal. A bill still open after those three notices can be offered to third-party companies, which buy it and place a lien against the land. No sales happen before August, and the list, with the sale date, is posted on the clerk's page as the day approaches.

Debt grows fast once a bill reaches the clerk. Penalty, the add-on fee and a commission are folded into the certificate, then 1 percent interest accrues monthly, with a 10 percent clerk commission and, after the first notice, a 20 percent county attorney commission. Paying within five business days of the transfer avoids the attorney's share.

Meeting with the PVA at Suite 6 is the entry point. PVAs value most houses by comparing recent sales, and your conference is the time to ask which sales were used. After the meeting you file with the clerk at the end of the next workday after the May viewing period, a stretch of two weeks that includes Saturdays. A board of local owners hears the case roughly a month afterward.

Come with facts: building characteristics, insurance values, construction costs or listings of similar property. Without them the board denies the appeal. A paid representative needs your written authorization and a recognized credential, for example an attorney, accountant, broker or appraiser.

Farmland follows a separate rule. Kentucky values it at what the land earns in agriculture rather than what it would sell for, which can cut a bill sharply near cities and matters less in rural areas where the two values sit close together. Taxable personal property is listed with the PVA by May 15.

Owners past 65, or classified as totally disabled by a federal agency or a retirement system, have $49,100 subtracted from the assessment for 2025 and 2026. File Form 62A350 at the PVA before December 31. A household gets one exemption even if both spouses qualify, and a purchaser must apply again after a sale.

Get the sheriff's exact payoff, then ask the clerk whether the parcel carries a certificate from an earlier year. Each year's tax is the January 1 owner's own debt, and a delinquent lien can follow the land for eleven years. When an outside company holds the bill, the money goes to that company instead of the clerk.

Visit Suite 7 for the current year and the clerk's office for anything older, then give both written figures to the closing agent. If you want to sell without repairs or showings, a cash buyer can accept the house as it stands and pay the tax balances out of your proceeds at closing. Compare the amount you would keep after payoffs, not just the offer.

Bring a photo ID and the parcel number to each office. Ask each one to put the amount in writing with an expiration date, since figures change as penalties and interest run. A fresh figure close to the closing date is the one the title agent will trust.

faqs.q: Where can I pay a Taylor County property tax bill?
faqs.a: At the sheriff's office, 203 North Court Street, Suite 7, or through the online portal for 2026 payments. Call (270) 465-4351 to confirm the amount.

faqs.q: When does a Taylor County bill turn delinquent?
faqs.a: On April 15 of the following year. The sheriff's file closes and the clerk takes over collection.

faqs.q: Will Taylor County sell my overdue tax bill to a company?
faqs.a: It can, after the three notices. No sales happen before August, and the buyer's lien then attaches to your property.

faqs.q: How do I apply for the homestead exemption in Taylor County?
faqs.a: Take Form 62A350 to the PVA at (270) 465-5811 before December 31. The home must be your residence on January 1, and you must qualify by age or disability.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Taylor County house with back taxes owed?
faqs.a: Yes. The payoff comes out of your sale money. Bring written payoffs from the sheriff and the clerk so the closing agent can clear every open year.
